title: How many degrees make a quarter turn?
description: A quarter turn is found as a quarter of three hundred and sixty and as half of a half turn, and both give ninety degrees. Keeko's doubt, that a quarter is one hundred and eighty, is broken by showing that four such parts overflow a full turn.
teaching_notes: One idea: a quarter turn is one of four equal parts of the full turn, which is also half of a half turn. Watch for children who give the half turn for the quarter.

source: The measure of a quarter circle is 1/4 of a full turn. The m
video_script.why: The child finds the quarter turn in two ways and sees that both give ninety degrees.
video_script.substitution: The book's semicircle folded in half into a quarter circle.
video_script.anchor: the book's semicircle folded in half into a quarter circle
video_script.wrong_answer: a quarter of three hundred and sixty is one hundred and eighty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a quarter of three hundred and sixty is one hundred and eighty. That is half of the full turn, and four parts of it would make seven hundred and twenty degrees, so the bubble is struck.
maths_rules: a quarter turn = 1/2 of a half turn = 180 / 2 = 90 degrees
a quarter of 360 is not 180: 180 is half of 360, and 4 x 180 = 720 is more than a full turn
video_script.design: The quarter circle stays on the board. The number ninety is written only in the answer beat.
